items.title: How Has Visa's Growth Story Changed?
items.summary: Visa's management tells its growth story differently than it did two years ago. That matters for your money. The shares cost 31 times a year of earnings, against 22.4 times for the S&P 500. A price that high assumes the growth keeps coming. One label that used to feature in Visa's results has faded. Which part of the business did Visa's management use to highlight in its quarterly results.

items.title: FIS Modernizes Retirement Recordkeeping With Cloud-Native Platform
items.summary: Fidelity National upgrades retirement recordkeeping with a cloud-native platform designed to boost scalability, automation and modern participant experiences.

items.title: FIS Has One Number to Hit Before the Dividend Story Gets More Interesting
items.summary: FIS carries a debt load that has frozen buybacks and rewritten its dividend history once already, and there is one internal metric that will determine whether income investors get a growth story or another reset.

items.title: Can Visa Stock Keep Climbing After The World Cup?
items.summary: Visa (V) stock has run well ahead of the market, returning 13.5% over the past three months against 4.2% for the S&P 500. It now trades about 4% below its 52-week high. The next leg depends less on card swipes than on the services Visa sells on top of its network, which now bring in almost a third of its revenue.

items.title: FIS (FIS) Stock May Look Reasonable Despite Record Banking Wins
items.summary: Fidelity National Information Services has seen its share price fall sharply in recent years, even as it continues to win large banking technology contracts. The question for investors is whether the current US$36.43 price fairly reflects what the company is earning today and what those earnings can support over time. items.title: How FIS' Core Banking Wins Point to Broader Growth Opportunities
items.summary: Fidelity National's recent core banking wins could deepen client relationships and open doors to more digital banking, payments, lending and data products.

items.title: Fidelity National Information Services Inc's Dividend Analysis
items.summary: Fidelity National Information Services Inc (NYSE:FIS) recently announced a total dividend of $0.44 per share, with the ex-dividend date set for 2026-09-11.  This amount includes a $0.44 per share cash dividend payable on 2026-09-25.  For income-focused investors, the ex-dividend date is a critical deadline: shareholders must own the stock before this date to qualify for the upcoming payment.

items.title: Is Visa Stock Expensive, Or Just Waiting On Its Margin?
items.summary: Visa (V) trades at about $367 a share. On the last twelve months of adjusted earnings, meaning normalized net income with stock-based compensation added back, that is about 28.6 times earnings. Nobody buys a payments network expecting a bargain. The question is whether the trailing multiple tells you what you are actually paying.
